problem: Prior VLN work handles behavioral diversity (backtracking, multi-hypothesis search, noise) and reliability/stability through separate mechanisms, often at inference time. The training-time interaction between them is left implicit, causing either early over-commitment or uncoordinated hypotheses.
motivation: Self-improvement from policy-induced experience under standard action supervision needs both diversity, to cover ambiguous instructions, and stable learning signals. Too much diversity destabilizes updates, while too much stability causes early commitment and suboptimal local optima. The paper therefore builds an explicit training-time expand-select operator that couples the two.
key_idea: A plug-in (1->K->1) operator between the backbone encoder and the action head that expands each step into K bounded low-rank latent hypotheses via hidden-state shifts, then softly fuses them with reliability (alignment/confidence/stability) weights under an explicit regularizer.
insight: Gains come from structured hypothesis generation plus reliability-aware consolidation, not from perturbation or more hypotheses. The NavGPT-2 R2R val_seen ablation shows HSG+Stable gives SR 75 / SPL 67, versus 71-72 / 64 for Noise or Rand combinations. K ablation on REVERIE shows a sweet spot at K=3 (SPL 35.93), with K=5 falling back to 34.90. On SOON, SDB improves SPL but slightly lowers SR/OSR, an efficiency-reachability trade-off.
method: State summary: masked mean pooling of instruction tokens T_t and environment tokens E_t plus a step embedding, passed through an MLP to give s_t.

Head-Shifting Generator (HSG): a shared low-rank shift basis B_t = W_u Diag(sigmoid(W_b s_t)) W_d (rank 32), softmax slot gating pi_t over K slots, and a cross-attention alignment residual with per-hypothesis query bias, scaled by a learnable gamma=sigmoid(theta). Slot 0 is the unshifted anchor; slots k>=1 get bounded shifts to the instruction tokens.

Hypothesis bank: a shared fusion block f_eta (one instruction-to-environment cross-attention layer plus FFN) turns each shifted instruction state and the shared environment evidence into hypothesis contexts H^(k).

Reliability evaluator (ACS): per hypothesis, alignment (cosine to the anchor), confidence (negative entropy of the action distribution from the shared head) and stability (cosine to the previous step's context) cues go through a small MLP to give a score, then softmax gives weights w_t.
Soft fusion / stable select: training feeds H_acs = sum_k w_k H^(k) to the policy. Execution commits to argmax of EMA-smoothed weights, with learnable rho.

SDB regularizer: L_agr (reliability-weighted pull toward the fused representation), L_sm (smoothness across neighbouring slots), and L_div (hinge on hypothesis variance with a learnable margin m). Total loss = L_duet + softplus(theta) * L_sdb.

setting.backbone: DUET (main), GOAT, NavGPT-2 (VLM-based) with SDB plug-in, trained
setting.training_data: Standard R2R/SOON/REVERIE action-label supervision only (DAgger-style imitation with SPL expert, 200k iterations); no extra data.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ViT-B/16 features) plus DUET global-map tokens and instruction text
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph candidate viewpoints plus STOP

numbers_note: Backbone-generality tables also give val-seen rows for GOAT (SR 81.87 / SPL 74.67) and NavGPT-2 (SR 75 / SPL 67), not listed above. R2R numbers for DUET are printed as integers.
results: DUET+SDB improves REVERIE val_unseen SPL 33.73->35.93, SR 46.98->50.81 and OSR 51.07->54.25 over DUET, and test_unseen SPL 36.06->37.74. It also lifts R2R SPL (60->62 val_unseen) and SOON SPL (22.58->25.00 val_unseen, with shorter TL), though SOON SR/OSR drop slightly. Gains also appear with GOAT (REVERIE val_unseen SPL 36.70->39.00) and NavGPT-2 (R2R val_unseen SR 70->71, SPL 59->60).
limitations: Gains are modest and on R2R often small (SR unchanged on val_unseen); SOON shows a drop in SR/OSR, and the paper only hypothesizes that reliability-driven consolidation encourages premature stopping.
Overhead grows roughly linearly with K, and the best K is dataset-dependent (K=2 is better on REVERIE val_seen), so it must be tuned.

Evidence relies on partially described ablations (seed robustness, ACS cue ablation not tabulated) and single-run numbers. The 'self-improvement' framing is essentially a training regularizer on supervised learning, without new on-policy data collection.
